en: The Eleven-faced One:
Oṃ, homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas!
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī, in the Karīra Grove.
Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, surrounded by a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of vidyādharas, approached the place where the Blessed One was.
Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated the Blessed One, and sat down to one side. He then addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"O Blessed One, this is my heart-mantra named 'Eleven Faces,' which was spoken over eleven hundred million eons.
If I were now to speak it for the sake, welfare, and happiness of all sentient beings— for the pacification of all diseases,
for the warding off of all evils, misfortunes, and bad dreams, for the warding off of all untimely deaths, and for those who lack faith— "

For the sake of propitiating all obstacles and *vināyakas*, and for their pacification— O Blessed One, I do not perceive anything in this world with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation of recluses and brahmins, by means of which [this] heart could [be surpassed].

When protection has been performed—when defense, guardianship, pacification, auspiciousness, the warding off of the staff, the warding off of weapons, and the elimination of poison have been accomplished—if anyone should transgress, it is impossible that it would not be pacified; for while the maturation of the ancient karma of those [beings] remains, there is no possibility otherwise.
However, for one who prepares this and places full faith in it, [that karma] will cease to exist in every respect and in all ways.
This heart-essence is praised by all Buddhas; this heart-essence is attended to by all Tathāgatas; this heart-essence is rejoiced in by all Tathāgatas.
Lord, I remember that more than as many eons ago as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges, there was a Tathāgata named Śatapadmanayanacūḍapratihataraṅgavelakiraṇarāja.
In the presence of that Tathāgata, I heard and mastered this heart-essence.

Simultaneously with its attainment, all the Tathāgatas in the ten directions become well-disposed toward one who has attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Thus, this *hṛdaya* is of great benefit; therefore, a faithful son of good family or daughter of good family should, with reverence, accomplish this *hṛdaya*.
One should accomplish this constantly with an undistracted mind.
Having risen at dawn, one should recite it one hundred and eight times.
Ten qualities pertaining to the present life are to be acquired.
What are the ten? Namely: he will be free from disease, and he will be sustained by all the Tathāgatas.
His wealth, grain, gold, and ornaments shall become inexhaustible;
all his enemies shall be subdued and crushed;
and in the royal assembly, he shall be considered the first to be addressed.
Neither poison, nor *gara*, nor fever, nor weapons shall take effect upon his body;
he shall not meet death by water,
nor shall he meet death by fire.
He shall not meet his end through untimely death;
furthermore, he will obtain four other qualities and benefits:
at the time of death, there will be a vision of the Tathāgata.
Nor will one be reborn in the states of woe; nor will one die by failing to avoid dangers;
having passed away from here, one will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī.

"I remember, Blessed One, that ten eons ago, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, and even further back than that, there was a Tathāgata named Mandāravagandha. There, while I was still a householder, I received this [teaching],
and for forty thousand eons I turned my back upon cyclic existence."
And by applying my heart to this, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the "Womb of Compassionate Wisdom.

Thus, for those who are bound in fetters, those who are subject to bondage, and those afflicted by the various sufferings of water and fire, through this I become a shelter, a protection, a refuge, and a final resort for all sentient beings.

"By means of this heart-mantra, having drawn in all wicked yakṣas and rākṣasas and made them possess minds of loving-kindness and compassion, I establish them in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Blessed One, when this heart-mantra of mine, which possesses such great supernatural power, is revealed even once, the four root transgressions go to destruction, and the five deeds of immediate retribution will be rendered completely attenuated."

How much more so for those who will practice according to what has been taught! They will have planted roots of merit under many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas; this applies even more so to those who [practice] through recitation, ritual accomplishments (*sādhana*), and so forth.
"I shall fulfill every desire of whoever observes a fast on the fourteenth or fifteenth day dedicated to me;
for forty thousand kalpas they shall turn their backs upon saṃsāra.
Blessed One, by merely grasping my name, such a person is equal to more than hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas."
By the mere grasping of my name, all sentient beings shall attain the state of non-retrogression;
they shall be completely liberated from all diseases,
and they shall be released from all obscurations, all fears, and all misdeeds of body, speech, and mind.
"The awakening of the Buddhas will be as if held in the palms of their very hands.
The Blessed One said:
"Excellent, excellent, noble son! That you possess such great compassion toward all sentient beings is wonderful.
Noble son, by this skillful means, you will be able to establish all sentient beings in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
I have received this heart-mantra and rejoice in it."
"Speak, son of good family!
Then the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One, and recited this heart-mantra:
"Homage to the Triple Gem."
Homage to Vairocana, the Tathāgata. Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One.
Homage to all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present.
Oṃ dhara dhara / dhiri dhiri / dhuru dhuru /
iṭṭe viṭṭe / cale cale / pracale pracale /
*Kusume kusumavare ili mili viṭi svāhā*. Thus is the root mantra.
Homage to the Triple Gem!
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara!
It is thus: hā hā hā hā.
*ime tile cile bhile khile svāhā*. This is the mantra for bathing, touching water, and sprinkling clothing; it is effective when recited seven times. *Namo ratnatrayāya*.
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
It is as follows: *ṭuru ṭuru hā hā hā hā svāhā*.
This is the mantra for the offering of incense and lamps.
Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara!
It is as follows: *thiri thiri dhiri dhiri svāhā*.
The mantra for the offering of incense and flowers:
Homage to the Three Jewels!
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One!
Namely: *sāde sāde sidi sidi sudu sudu svāhā*. This is the mantra for the offering of the bali-oblation; it should be recited twenty-one times. *Namo ratnatrayāya* (Homage to the Three Jewels).
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One. It is as follows: yasi ddhasi cari huru icuruḥ suruḥ muruḥ svāhā.
The *homamantra*:

with this mantra, having kindled the fire with the eight [kinds of] wood of the kinsmen, one should perform thirty oblations (*homa*) during a single day and night, using [fuel sticks] anointed with curd, honey, and ghee.
Then one should begin the ritual action:
Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Greatly Compassionate One!
It is as follows: *ili mili tili tili hili svāhā*.
A lamp that is about to go out may be rekindled by means of water, ashes, or by reciting the mantra seven times:
"Homage to the Triple Gem!
Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One!"
Namely: *piṭi piṭi tiṭi tiṭi viṭi viṭi gaccha gaccha bhagavān āryāvalokiteśvara svabhavanaṃ svabhavanaṃ svāhā*.
Having recited this seven times over water, one should sprinkle it in the four directions, saying:
"Noble Avalokiteśvara, go to your own abode!"
